chunks: And Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Bawari narrated to me, saying: Yusuf ibn Ya'qub al-Muqri' al-Saqti narrated to me in Wasit, saying: Khalaf al-Bazzar narrated to me, from Yazeed ibn Harun, from Hameed at-Taweel, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying:
Do not tell people of what they do not know. Do you like for Allah and His Messenger to be considered liars?

key_terms.أَنَسُ بْنُ مَالِكٍ: Anas ibn Malik, a companion of the Prophet
key_terms.يُكَذَّبَ: to be considered a liar / to be accused of falsehood

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of telling people what they do not know in Islamic ethics?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Anas ibn Malik, emphasizes the principle of *al-ghayba* (concealment) crucial to Shia theology, particularly regarding the Imam's hidden status, warning against publicizing matters beyond the audience's capacity to comprehend. By linking this to the risk of *kathib Allah wa Rasuluhu* (accusing God and His Messenger of falsehood), it highlights how premature or misunderstood revelation can lead to doubt in the divine message. This context is vital for understanding the strategic silence of the Ahl al-Bayt during periods of political and theological persecution.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (2) Abul Qassim al-Husayn bin Muhammad al-Bawari narrated from Yousuf bin Ya’qoob al-Muqri’ as-Saqti from Khalaf al-Bazzaz from Yazeed bin Haroon from Hameed at-Taweel that Anass bin Malik had said: “I heard the Prophet (S) saying: “
Do not tell people of what they do not know. Do you like Allah and His messenger to be considered as liars?”
